title: Know your margin
principle: Know your margin on every item you sell.

screens.text: Raju sells biscuits and loose namkeen. Both sell well. Only one pays his rent.

screens.title: Margin
screens.text: Margin is what you keep from one sale: the price minus what the item cost you.

screens.prompt: A biscuit pack costs Raju ₹9. He sells it for ₹10. What is his margin?
screens.why: ₹10 price minus ₹9 cost leaves ₹1 a pack.
Branded packs earn little. Loose and home-made items earn more.

screens.prompt: Which item should get the front shelf?

options.label: Namkeen, because it earns more each sale

screens.why: The front shelf sells the most. Give it to what earns the most.

steps: Write down what each item costs
See which items earn the most
screens.why: First the cost, then the margin, then the shelf.

summary: Margin is price minus cost, for one sale.
Give your best space to high-margin items.

cards.front: Chai costs you ₹8 a cup. You sell it for ₹10. Your margin?
One item sells fast at ₹1 margin. One sells slower at ₹5. Which gets the front shelf?
cards.back: Usually the ₹5 one: each sale earns five times more.
